cards.explanation: The answer is leaders of the people. Verse 1 says it plainly: Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah "…were leaders of the people." Out of twenty-five men at that gate, these are the two the text names. What the LORD says about these men comes next, and it's serious.

The two words are plot and wicked. The LORD says, "…these are the men who plot evil and give wicked counsel in this city." Plotting is planning ahead, and here the plan is evil. God tells Ezekiel, the prophet in this vision, exactly what these men are doing, so nothing is hidden from Him. Counsel just means advice, and advice from the wrong people gets expensive fast.

The answer is False. The LORD does not tell Ezekiel to keep quiet, and He says it twice. Verse 4 says, "Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, O son of man!" Ezekiel isn't told to keep quiet. He's told to speak, and he does.

The answer is True. God says in verse 5, "…I know the thoughts that arise in your minds." He's speaking to the house of Israel, and He knows what goes on in their minds. Friends, I can walk into my kitchen and forget why I came in. God never loses track of a single thought.

The answer is the slain laid within the city. The men said, "The city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat." Then verse 7 says, "The slain you have laid within this city are the meat, and the city is the pot; but I will remove you from it." God uses the same picture, puts the slain in it, and says the men will be removed.

The answer is False. God says He will not leave these men in the city. In verse 7 God says, "but I will remove you from it." Verse 11 adds, "The city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be the meat within it." They're headed out.

The answer is the sword. Verse 8 says, "You fear the sword, so I will bring the sword against you, declares the Lord GOD." What they feared is exactly what God says He will bring. This is a heavy part of the passage.

The word is nations. In verse 12 God says, "For you have neither followed My statutes nor practiced My ordinances, but you have conformed to the ordinances of the nations around you." God had given them His ordinances. They took the ones from the nations around them instead.
The answer is that he dies. Ezekiel says in verse 13, "Now as I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died." Pelatiah is one of the two leaders named at the gate. This is a heavy moment.

The answer is that Ezekiel asks whether God will bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end. He falls facedown and cries, "Oh, Lord GOD, will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end?" I think this is a prayer from a man shaken by what just happened. The next thing in the text is the word of the LORD coming to him.

The answer is that they are far away from the LORD. That's what the people of Jerusalem say in verse 15: "They are far away from the LORD…" They were talking about Ezekiel's brothers, his relatives and fellow exiles. God repeats what was said, so He heard every word of it.

The answer is True. Verse 15 says the people of Jerusalem said, "this land has been given to us as a possession." They said it about themselves, right after saying the exiles were far from the LORD. God tells Ezekiel what they said, and then He answers it.

The word is sanctuary. God says, "…yet for a little while I have been a sanctuary for them in the countries to which they have gone." A sanctuary is a place of safety and nearness. The people in Jerusalem said the exiles were far from the LORD, and God's answer is that He has been a sanctuary for them even there.

The word is land. Verse 17 says, "I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries to which you have been scattered, and I will give back to you the land of Israel." The people of Jerusalem said the land was theirs. God says He'll give it back to the exiles.

The answer is False. God says in verse 18, "When they return to it, they will remove all its detestable things and all its abominations." The exiles come back and clear the place out. Nothing detestable gets left on the shelf.

The heart God removes is a heart of stone. He says, "I will remove their heart of stone and give them a heart of flesh…" (Ezekiel 11:19) Stone doesn't bend, and God takes it out. This is the promise God makes about the exiles' hearts.
The word is flesh. God says, "I will remove their heart of stone and give them a heart of flesh…" A heart of flesh is the opposite of stone. It's a heart God gives, not one they make.

The answer is so they may follow His statutes. Verse 20 says, "…so that they may follow My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them." Earlier, God said the men at the gate hadn't followed His statutes. Here He gives the exiles a new heart and a new spirit so that they can.

The answer is True. God says it word for word in verse 20: "Then they will be My people, and I will be their God." It comes right after the new heart and the following of His statutes. This is the promise God makes to the exiles.

The word is east. Verse 23 says, "And the glory of the LORD rose up from within the city and stood over the mountain east of the city." The glory had stopped at the east gate of the house of the LORD earlier in the vision (Ezekiel 10:19). Now it rises from within the city and stands over the mountain to the east.

The answer is that he tells them everything the LORD showed him. Verse 25 has Ezekiel saying, "I told the exiles everything the LORD had shown me." He doesn't hold a single piece back. A vision like this, the gate, the pot, the new heart and the glory rising, goes straight to the exiles.
